rule.title: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) for Functions
rule.statement: Every function and method must perform a single, well-defined task and operate at a consistent level of abstraction.
rule.rationale: Functions that mix business decisions with data formatting and low-level I/O are difficult to test, impossible to reuse, and attract bugs during changes.
rule.implementation_guidance: If a function contains 'and' in its informal description (e.g. 'parseAndSaveAndNotify'), split it into distinct composed functions.

forbidden.example: function process(buffer) { /* 200 lines doing regex, embedding, db calls, and emails */ }

preferred.example: const text = extractText(buffer); const chunks = splitIntoChunks(text); await storeChunks(chunks);

source.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
source.evidence_quote: Functions should do one thing. They should do it well. They should do it only. If a function does only those steps that are one level below the stated name, it does one thing.

rule.title: Small Function Size and Guard Clause Early Returns
rule.statement: Functions should not exceed 40 lines of logic and must use guard clauses (early returns) to maintain a cyclomatic nesting depth of 3 or less.
rule.rationale: Deeply nested if-else ladders increase cognitive complexity exponentially, leading to missed edge cases and maintenance dread.
rule.implementation_guidance: Check preconditions at the top of the function and return immediately on failure. Avoid else blocks after returns.

forbidden.example: if (user) { if (hasAccess(user)) { ... } else { ... } } else { ... } // Arrow anti-pattern

source.book_title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
source.evidence_quote: Functions should hardly ever be 20 lines long... the indent level of a function should not be greater than one or two.
